fix: Keep a snapshot in FormRegistry: add `listener_snapshot: Rc<[Rc<dyn Fn()>]>`, rebuild it only in add_listener and remove_listener (rare), and in notify_form_listeners take `let listeners = Rc::clone(&state.listener_snapshot);` (inside the existing borrow_mut block) then `for listener in listeners.iter() { listener(); }`. Every field edit calls this (via the controller observer at line 172), so the per-notification Vec goes away. Snapshot semantics (listeners removed mid-pass still run once) are unchanged.

Use `listeners: BTreeMap<usize, Rc<dyn Fn()>>` (add BTreeMap to the collections import; HashMap stays for `fields`). Listener tokens are monotonically increasing, so iteration becomes deterministic registration order instead of per-process random HashMap order. Pairs with the snapshot fix at line 524.

Add `fn has_error_entry(&self) -> bool;` to the private FormEntry trait, implement it as `self.error.borrow().is_some()` in FieldState and GenericFieldState, and write `let all_error_free = fields.iter().all(|(_, field)| !field.has_error_entry());`. Today each field's error String is cloned only to test for None.

Count without building and sorting a Vec: `let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut(); state.changes.track(); state.fields.retain(|_, field| field.strong_count() > 0); state.fields.len()`. This keeps the prune side effect and dependency tracking of live_fields, with no allocation or sort. Callers that read it during build are the hot case.

Compare without cloning the text on every build: `let text_changed = controller.with_value(|value| self.last_text.borrow().as_deref() != Some(value.text.as_str()));`. Then fetch the owned value only when text changed: `if text_changed && !self.selecting.get() { let value = controller.value(); ... }` (and similarly `else if text_changed { let value = controller.value(); ... }`). controller.value() (editing.rs:401) clones the String; with_value (editing.rs:409) does not. Do not call build_options inside with_value, since the callback may reenter the controller.

Store the fixed options as `Rc<[T]>` (in RawAutocomplete and RawAutocompleteState) and have build_options return `Rc<[T]>`: `None => Rc::clone(&self.options)`, `Some(builder) => builder(value).into()`. Today every text change deep-clones the whole fixed options Vec<T> even though it never changes. Pairs with the layout clone finding at line 1037.

Change RawAutocompleteState.options from `RefCell<Vec<T>>` to `RefCell<Rc<[T]>>` (sync at line 880 stores `Rc::from(...)`, or the build_options change above). Then line 1037 becomes `let options = Rc::clone(&state.options.borrow());`. The overlay_child_layout_builder closure at lines 1057-1058 runs during overlay layout and currently does `(view.clone(), select.clone(), options.clone())`, which deep-clones the whole Vec<T> on every layout pass while the options are showing; with Rc<[T]> that is a refcount bump. Also consider hoisting the `Rc::default()` passed to Widget::stateful_builder at line 1061 into a field of the captured state if that API allows, since it allocates per layout pass.

Skip segmentation when it cannot matter: `if enforce && value.text.len() > self.max_length { let end = ...; value.text.truncate(end); }`. A grapheme cluster is at least one byte, so text no longer than max_length bytes holds at most max_length clusters and the `nth(self.max_length)` lookup would find nothing and truncate to no change. The current code segments the whole text on every edit (keystroke) even for short text.
